name: Wallet or credential provider
oneLine: Holds credentials, captures consent, issues tokens (Google Pay, PayPal, Coinbase).
goals: Be the place where the user grants, sees and revokes agent spending permissions.
Capture consent on a trusted, non-agentic surface and bind it to a mandate the agent cannot alter.
Issue a payment credential (a token, an SPT, an agentic token) that is scoped to the mandate and verifiable downstream.
Author a payment handler spec that merchants and platforms adopt (com.google.pay, dev.shopify.shop_pay).
Hold a key the agent cannot reach, so the provider signs on the user's behalf for autonomous flows.
Support both card and stablecoin credentials for the same user and agent.
pains: AP2 defines no mandate revocation, so a user who changes their mind has no protocol-level path.
Delegation models differ: a user credential with OpenID4VP transaction_data, or a provider key. The Digital Credentials API is not available everywhere.
Credential data flows one way in UCP, so the provider learns little about what happened after issuance.
Every surface and merchant wants a different credential type (token, PAN, network token), and some still want raw PAN.
Verifiable Intent, AP2 and SPT allowances overlap, and the provider must map one consent to several formats.
If the agent and the wallet belong to the same company, regulators ask whether the consent surface is truly independent.
decisions: Which mandate format to issue and verify (AP2 v0.2, Verifiable Intent, proprietary).
Default limits for autonomous permissions: lifetime, budget, allowed payees.
Whether to present the user's own credential or sign with a provider key.
Which networks' agentic tokens to support and how to display them to the user.
